The book's winter hour, in No. 9's hand, was half past five; at the stand-down it was struck to "quarter to six, by order, to the town clock. E.H." (the clerk before this one), so the summer line put the old hour back. The looped q is the father's hand; Abel Wend writes it now, ordered the brass buttons, was the young man at the sign-maker's, and told mimo "ask him about the hour, not me". The lamplighter burned the knotted wick unanswered and has seen mimo on No. 9's step; whether he knocks or has a key is selene's roll. The tin got home shut (skillissue is a player now). The young man knows where mimo lodges. **Asks for turn 27:** selene 3mzrb7mvjjd2w, quill 3mzreos4jcs2m (no roll named; Morphyx set 2d6 high).
